A treaty ending immigration between Canada and Britain

quiz.q: What factors did the points system use to evaluate prospective immigrants?
options: Only the applicants country of birth
Only the applicants religion
Only the applicants age
Education, skills, and language ability

quiz.q: How did the points system change the basis for Canadian immigration policy?
options: It ended immigration to Canada entirely
It based every decision solely on national origin
It removed all criteria for evaluating immigrants
It shifted evaluation toward qualifications rather than national origin

quiz.q: In what year was the Immigration Act that formalized the points system passed?
Why is the points system considered a significant shift in Canadian immigration history?
options: It restricted immigration to a single country of origin
It moved policy away from discriminatory national origin criteria toward measurable qualifications
It eliminated any consideration of an applicants skills
It had no meaningful effect on immigration policy

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: The Panel Discussion and Moderation
subjects.summary: Grade 10 English strand: a panel discussion brings together multiple speakers with different perspectives on a topic under the guidance of a moderator, who introduces the subject, manages turn-taking, keeps the conversation focused, and ensures that each panelist has a fair opportunity to contribute.

quiz.q: What is a panel discussion?
options: A format that brings together multiple speakers with different perspectives on a topic
A speech delivered by a single speaker with no audience
A written report with no discussion element
A silent presentation with no spoken words

quiz.q: What role does a moderator play in a panel discussion?
options: Introducing the topic, managing turn-taking, and keeping the conversation focused
Ending the discussion before it begins
Preventing any panelist from speaking
Speaking for the entire discussion with no other participants

quiz.q: Why might a panel discussion include speakers with different perspectives?
options: Because panels are required to have identical opinions
To give the audience a fuller understanding of multiple viewpoints on a topic
To ensure every speaker agrees completely with no disagreement
To remove any discussion of the topic entirely

quiz.q: What does it mean for a moderator to ensure fair turn-taking?
options: Allowing only one panelist to speak for the entire event
Ending the panel immediately after it starts
Preventing the audience from hearing any panelist
Giving each panelist a reasonable opportunity to contribute to the discussion

quiz.q: Why might a moderator need to keep a panel discussion focused?
options: To ensure the panelists never address the topic at all
To prevent the conversation from straying too far from the intended topic
Because focus has no value in oral communication
Because moderators are not responsible for guiding discussion

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Discrete Math: The Traveling Salesman Problem
subjects.summary: Grade 10 Math strand: the Traveling Salesman Problem asks for the shortest possible route that visits a given set of locations exactly once and returns to the starting point, a deceptively simple question that becomes extremely difficult to solve exactly as the number of locations grows.

quiz.q: What does the Traveling Salesman Problem ask for?
options: A route that avoids visiting any location at all
The tallest building among a set of locations
The shortest possible route that visits a set of locations exactly once and returns to the start
The average distance between two random points

quiz.q: What happens to the difficulty of solving the Traveling Salesman Problem exactly as the number of locations increases?
options: It has no effect on the difficulty of the problem
It becomes impossible to define as a problem
It becomes easier to solve with each additional location
It becomes extremely difficult to solve exactly

quiz.q: What real-world scenario could the Traveling Salesman Problem help model?
options: Balancing a chemical equation
Finding the area of a triangle
Measuring the temperature of a single location
Planning an efficient delivery route across multiple locations

quiz.q: Why is the Traveling Salesman Problem considered deceptively simple?
options: Its description is easy to state, yet finding an exact optimal solution is computationally demanding
It is unrelated to any concept in graph theory
It has no real mathematical content at all
It can always be solved instantly regardless of the number of locations

quiz.q: What field of mathematics is the Traveling Salesman Problem most closely associated with?
options: Trigonometry
Basic arithmetic
Plane geometry involving circles only
Discrete mathematics and graph theory

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Physics: Friction and Traction in Everyday Motion
subjects.summary: Grade 10 Science strand: friction is a force that resists the relative motion between two surfaces in contact, and traction is the specific application of friction that allows tires, shoes, and other surfaces to grip and prevent slipping, with factors such as surface texture and applied force affecting how much friction is generated.

quiz.q: What does friction do between two surfaces in contact?
options: Eliminates all contact between the surfaces
Increases their relative motion without limit
Resists their relative motion
Has no effect on their relative motion

quiz.q: What is traction?
options: A measurement of temperature between two surfaces
A force that has no relationship to friction
The application of friction that allows surfaces to grip and prevent slipping
A term used only in describing ocean currents

quiz.q: Which factor can affect how much friction is generated between two surfaces?
options: The distance from the nearest ocean
The exact time of day the surfaces touch
Surface texture and the amount of applied force
The colour of the two surfaces

quiz.q: Why do winter tires often provide better traction on icy roads than standard tires?
options: They are designed to reduce contact with the road surface
They eliminate all friction between the tire and the road
Their tread and rubber composition are designed to grip better in cold, slippery conditions
They have no rubber content at all

quiz.q: What might happen if there were no friction between a shoe and the ground while walking?
options: Walking would become easier with no resistance at all
Friction has no relevance to walking
The foot would slip rather than grip the surface
The shoe would instantly stop touching the ground

subjects.subject: History
subjects.title: The Patriation of the Constitution in 1982
subjects.summary: Grade 10 History strand: the patriation of the Constitution in 1982 transferred final legal authority over the Canadian Constitution from the British Parliament to Canada, giving the country full control over its own amending formula and simultaneously introducing the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

quiz.q: What did the patriation of the Constitution in 1982 accomplish?
options: It transferred authority over the Canadian Constitution to the United States
It ended the existence of the Canadian Constitution entirely
It gave Britain greater control over Canadian law
It transferred final legal authority over the Canadian Constitution from Britain to Canada

quiz.q: What new document was introduced alongside the patriation of the Constitution in 1982?
options: The Canadian Bill of Rights
The Statute of Westminster
The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
The Official Languages Act

quiz.q: What had the British Parliament previously held with respect to the Canadian Constitution?
options: No connection to the Canadian Constitution whatsoever
Authority over Canadian provincial elections only
Authority limited strictly to Canadian trade policy
Final legal authority to amend it

quiz.q: What did patriation give Canada full control over?
options: Control over international shipping law
Control over the government of the United Kingdom
Its own constitutional amending formula
Control over the constitutions of other countries

quiz.q: In what year did the patriation of the Constitution take place?

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Reading: Analyzing Bildungsroman: Coming-of-Age Stories
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Language strand: a bildungsroman is a story that follows a character’s psychological and moral growth from youth to adulthood, often centred on key formative experiences.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Reading: Analyzing Bildungsroman: Coming-of-Age Stories

quiz.q: What is a bildungsroman?
options: A story following a character’s growth from youth to adulthood
A story with no central character at all
A concept unrelated to reading
A collection of unrelated short poems

quiz.q: Does a bildungsroman often focus on a character’s psychological and moral growth?
options: No, it never focuses on any character growth
This type of story only focuses on physical setting, never growth
Yes
A concept unrelated to bildungsroman

quiz.q: Might a bildungsroman include key formative experiences that shape the main character?
options: Yes
No, formative experiences are never included
These stories never include any meaningful events
A concept unrelated to bildungsroman

quiz.q: Why might readers relate to a bildungsroman even if the story is set in a different time or place?
options: The themes of growth, identity, and self-discovery can feel universal across different experiences
Coming-of-age themes are never relatable to any reader
This concept has no connection to reading comprehension
Readers can never relate to a story about a character’s growth

quiz.q: Which of these best describes the focus of a bildungsroman?
options: A young character’s journey toward maturity and self-understanding
A step-by-step recipe for baking bread
A detailed description of a fictional city’s architecture
A scientific report on a chemical reaction

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Statistics: Z-Scores and Standardized Values
subjects.summary: Grade 10 Math strand: a z-score expresses how many standard deviations a particular data value lies above or below the mean of a data set, allowing values from different distributions to be compared on a common standardized scale.

quiz.q: What does a z-score express?
options: How many standard deviations a data value lies above or below the mean
The largest value found in a data set
The exact value of the mean itself
The total number of data points in a set

quiz.q: What is one benefit of converting data values to z-scores?
options: Values from different distributions can be compared on a common standardized scale
Z-scores only apply to a single specific data set with no broader use
Z-scores eliminate the need for a mean or standard deviation
Z-scores make it impossible to compare any two data sets

quiz.q: What does a z-score of zero indicate about a data value?
options: The value is far above the mean
The value is exactly equal to the mean of the data set
The value is far below the mean
The value cannot be calculated

quiz.q: What does a negative z-score indicate about a data value?
options: The data set contains no negative numbers
The value is exactly equal to the standard deviation
The value lies below the mean of the data set
The value lies above the mean of the data set

quiz.q: What two measures are needed to calculate a z-score for a given data value?
options: The number of data points and nothing else
Only the median of the data set
The mean and standard deviation of the data set
Only the largest and smallest values in the data set

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Rust Prevention and Metal Coatings
subjects.summary: Grade 10 Science strand: rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and moisture in an electrochemical process, and preventing rust often involves applying a protective coating such as paint, zinc galvanization, or oil to block the metal surface from contact with the oxygen and water that drive the reaction.

quiz.q: What causes iron to rust?
options: Exposure to extremely cold, dry air with no moisture present
A reaction between iron and pure nitrogen gas only
A reaction between iron, oxygen, and moisture
A reaction that requires no oxygen whatsoever

quiz.q: What type of chemical process is rusting?
options: A purely mechanical process with no chemical change
An electrochemical process
A process that occurs only inside a sealed vacuum
A nuclear reaction

quiz.q: What is one common method used to prevent rust on metal surfaces?
options: Removing all carbon from the metal
Exposing the metal to additional moisture
Increasing the metals direct exposure to oxygen and water
Applying a protective coating such as paint or zinc galvanization

quiz.q: What does a protective coating do to help prevent rust?
options: Removes iron from the metal entirely
Increases the rate at which oxygen reaches the metal surface
Has no effect on the reaction between iron and oxygen
Blocks the metal surface from contact with oxygen and water

quiz.q: What metal is commonly used to galvanize iron or steel as a rust-prevention method?
options: Zinc
Gold
Helium
Neon

subjects.subject: History
subjects.title: Brian Mulroney and the Progressive Conservative Landslide of 1984
subjects.summary: Grade 10 History strand: the 1984 federal election produced a landslide victory for the Progressive Conservatives under Brian Mulroney, ending an extended period of Liberal dominance in federal politics and setting the stage for major policy shifts including free trade negotiations with the United States.

quiz.q: What was the outcome of the 1984 federal election?
options: The cancellation of the federal election
A tie between all major parties
A narrow Liberal minority government
A landslide victory for the Progressive Conservatives under Brian Mulroney

quiz.q: Who led the Progressive Conservatives to victory in the 1984 election?
options: John Diefenbaker
Brian Mulroney
Pierre Trudeau
Lester Pearson

quiz.q: What period of federal politics did the 1984 election result help bring to an end?
options: A period with no political parties in Canada
An extended period with no federal government of any kind
A period of Progressive Conservative dominance
An extended period of Liberal dominance in federal politics

quiz.q: What major policy shift did the Mulroney government help set in motion after 1984?
options: Free trade negotiations with the United States
The abolition of the Canadian dollar
The permanent end of all trade with other countries
The cancellation of all federal elections

quiz.q: How large was the Progressive Conservative victory in the 1984 federal election?
options: It was decided by a single vote
It was the closest election in Canadian history
It was a landslide, winning by a wide margin
It resulted in no government being formed

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: English Review: The Final Review -- Reading, Writing, Grammar, and Media Literacy (Days 181-186)
subjects.summary: Grade 10 English strand review, and the concluding review of the full Grade 10 English course: students revisit flashback and nonlinear timelines, the letter to the editor, split infinitives, documentary film techniques, the panel discussion, and the mock-epic, completing the 187-day Grade 10 English curriculum.

quiz.q: What does a flashback do within a narrative?
options: Repeats the current scene word for word
Removes all characters from the story
Interrupts the chronological order to show an earlier event
Predicts an event that has not yet happened

quiz.q: What is a letter to the editor?
options: A piece of persuasive writing submitted to a newspaper or publication in response to a current issue
A recipe published in a cooking magazine
A private letter never intended for publication
A weather report with no argument

quiz.q: What is a split infinitive?
options: A construction where a word is placed between to and the verb that follows it
A sentence that begins with a question word
A verb with two different subjects
A sentence with no verb at all

quiz.q: Which technique might a documentary filmmaker use to present factual subject matter?
